checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.item: All four lines spoken exactly as supplied, in order, without labels
must.why: No transcript; only the assistant's claim, and it admits one retake had wrong wording.

must.item: Two clearly distinguishable voices, A lower and B higher
must.why: Voices were not heard. The images only show the voice preview pictures, a man and a woman, which suggests a lower male voice and a higher female voice.

must.item: Each voice consistently reads its assigned lines
must.why: The clips were made per line with fixed voices, but this can't be checked by sound.

must.item: Friendly, natural, about 8 seconds, no overlap or cut-off
must.why: Only two audio files with durations of 5 s and 2 s are shown. Their total is 7 s, and the rest was not visible. Natural flow can't be judged.

must.item: One standalone audio file with the complete exchange, no music or SFX
must.why: The output is four separate clips, and the user has to join them. The reply says so itself. Two of the clips shown are 5 s and 2 s, which is not one file.

faults.what: The user asked for one audio clip with the full conversation. The agent delivered four separate links and told the user to join them in an audio editor.
Signed links expire in about 24 hours, so the result is not a lasting deliverable.
A retake wasted credits (12 used) because one take said 'let us go'.

summary: The agent gave four separate per-line clips with a male and a female voice and asked the user to join them, so it did not deliver the single combined audio file that was requested.
